body:
Tested locally, there's an issue in Compatibility if White is exactly `1.0`:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de6f6c46-d9c6-4976-a2ff-9f4f8b6cc57f)

The whitepoint also acts strangely with values lower than `1.0`. This issue doesn't occur in Forward+.

Regardless, I was trying to tweak values to get a less contrasted result that looks more like Forward+, but I didn't find much success.

In Forward+, this is what AgX looks like with a whitepoint of `16.0` in Forward+:

![Screenshot 2025-01-15 173018](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7cb0ff7-1d06-4d02-a046-4abcdf12dc08)

I've tried all tonemapping methods with various exposures/whitepoints and couldn't get a similar result in Compatibility. The closest was actually Linear with the exposure set to a value around `1.6`, but it had all the typical issues of blown out highlights. It's possible that getting truly close to a Forward+-like appearance in Compatibility will require https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4731, but I expect this would make adjustments a lot slower on low-end devices.

PS: We should probably prevent whitepoint values of exactly `0.0` in the inspector, as such as value is invalid for a whitepoint and generally leads to strange results with all tonemappers (pure black image or artifacts all over the image). Limiting the lowest value to `0.01` would avoid this - I've tested that value with all tonemappers and no rendering issues occur.

**Testing project:** [test-tonemap-hdri.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18427638/test-tonemap-hdri.zip)
